page_01.text: The portal swallowed the light behind me, and for a moment there was nothing at all.
Then the world came back, but it was not my world anymore.
There is no sky I would call a sky, only a slow, deep colour high above,
like the bottom of a lake seen from below.
The grass glows, the stones glow, the water glows, and all of it from beneath,
as if the light rises out of the ground instead of falling onto it.
Every breath feels like the moment just before waking.
I have never seen anything so beautiful, and I have never felt so far from home.
I am writing this down so that I remember the way back.
I will need to remember the way back.

page_02.text: It came at me the moment it saw me, and I did what anyone would do.
Now it lies still, and I cannot stop looking at it.
It looks like the creatures from home, but wrong,
as if someone drew it from memory and forgot the important parts.
Cyan light leaks from cracks in its body like water from a broken jar.
And the way it looked at me, just before it attacked.
Not like an animal looks at prey.
Like I was someone it used to know, or someone it was waiting for.
I tell myself that is the strangeness of this place playing tricks on me.
I tell myself many things lately.

page_03.text: I know what you saw down there, and I know how it called to you.
The light, the warm air, the feeling that the world is breathing with you.
This place keeps what it is given, and it has been given so much already.
Every step you take down there is a step it remembers.
That little shifter in your hand opens a door in both directions,
and not everything that passes through it is you.
If you cross again, you cross on your own account.

page_04.text: There is something in the air down here that you can almost hold.
I call it Somnium, the stuff that dreams are made of.
Today I learned to hold it.
On that old table of stone,
the one that was already waiting here as if it had been waiting for me,
I bound a little of it into a ring.
When it closed around my finger, I felt the whole world breathe in and out,
and for one moment I knew exactly where every living thing around me was.
It did not feel like power.
I sat there for a long time afterwards, turning the ring in the glow.
I did not think about home once.
I only noticed that later, and it frightened me less than it should have.

page_05.text: I know now where the glow comes from.
They hang from the ceiling of this cave like the veins of something enormous,
thick and warm and slowly pulsing, and they do not end here.
They run beneath everything, under every forest, under every mountain,
under the very ground I have been sleeping on.
The light does not come from the plants.
I put my hand on one of the roots, and I felt a heartbeat.
Slow, patient, much older than me.
And for a moment it felt as if something on the other side of the bark had put its hand against mine as well.

page_06.text: That wolf followed someone through the border once.
It slept at their feet and growled at the dark for them.
Then they stayed too long, both of them,
and the roots took what they were and left what you just killed.
Every creature you have fought down here once stood where you stand now.
The hounds, the cattle, the walking dead, the great old beasts of the lowlands.
None of them were born in this world.
They came through the same border you did.
Look at them closely next time, before you raise your weapon.
Then ask yourself how long you have already stayed.

page_07.text: Of some of them, almost nothing is left.
This one drifted through the mist in a ragged hood, and when it stopped, it knelt,
as if it still remembered how to pray.
It attacked me with light that burned like poison.
When it fell, it did not scream.
It sighed, the way you sigh when you finally put down something heavy.
What was it praying for, all this time?
Did it pray to go home, or did it pray to stay?
I cannot get the sound of that sigh out of my head.
I wonder which of the two I would pray for, if I knelt like that.

page_08.text: I pushed the ring too far today.
I kept casting until there was nothing left in me,
until the Somnium was gone and my hands went cold and the world turned grey at the edges.
And in that silence, where the hum of this place should have been,
A quiet voice, very kind, from somewhere far below.
It said I did not have to be afraid of being empty,
that it would always fill me up again.
It told me the Abyss did not always look like this,
that it was once whole and bright and free.
It told me someone broke it.
Someone with a black blade, who keeps everything here locked away in the dark.
When the Somnium came back, the voice was gone.
But I can still feel where it was,
like warmth on a stone after the sun has set.

page_09.text: You died down there, and you came back.
That is what the roots want, do you understand?
Every time you fall and rise again,
a little less of you comes back and a little more of them.
I have watched it happen to others before you.
The voice will tell you that you are strong, that the Abyss has chosen you.
It told me the same thing, a long time ago.

page_10.text: A soft cyan, just beneath the skin,
running along the veins like light poured into a riverbed.
It started the moment the Somnium settled in me, and it has not faded since.
If anything, it feels warm, the way the roots feel warm.
The voice says it is a gift, a sign that this world has accepted me.
It says the creatures fear the light because they know what it means.
I keep my hand in my sleeve when I sleep,
so I do not have to look at it.
I am not sure what I am afraid of seeing.
I think I believe the voice.
It is easier to believe it.

page_11.text: It was enormous, a beast from a time older than any story I know,
with a jaw like the mouth of a cave and a tail that swept the ground clean.
It roared until the mist shook,
and it fought like something that had been fighting for a very long time.
When it finally fell, the earth trembled,
and the roots beneath it flared so brightly that I had to look away.
Then the light flowed out of it and back into the ground, slowly,
Nothing in this world is ever truly finished, I think.
It only returns to the roots.
I stood there long after the light was gone, and the strangest thought came to me.
I was not sad that I had killed it.
I was sad that it had stopped being mine to fight.

page_12.text: The key of ice opened a world that is quiet in a way the Abyss never is.
Snow, frozen spiders, knights of ice that stand still for years.
I could feel it the moment I arrived, the warmth gone from beneath my feet,
the hum gone from the back of my head.
For the first time since I crossed, my thoughts were only my own.
That is the truth, and I want to write it down while I still can.
I did not like the silence.

page_13.text: I built pillars like these once, long ago,
when I still believed the power down here could be shaped without shaping me.
Every spark of Somnium you bind to your will binds a little of your will to the roots.
I see the light in your hand from far away now.
It is brighter than mine ever was.
I was once where you are now.
I chose to stand against it, and I have stood ever since,
between this place and yours, so that nothing from below follows you home.
If you go on like this, I will have to stop you.

page_14.text: Or it let me find it.
An altar of dark stone, surrounded by pillars, old and silent and waiting.
The voice is loud now, louder than it has ever been.
It says this is where the one with the black blade can be called.
It says the pillars must burn first, each one fed with a heart full of souls,
and then the eye must be given to the altar.
I do not know how I know what the voice means.
Standing here, I can feel something watching me, the way it has watched me all along,
from the edges of the mist, from the corners of my eye.
Tall, dark, cracks of cyan light running across its body like a map of rivers.
The voice says this is the one who broke the Abyss.
It says that when it falls, everything down here will finally be free.

page_15.text: Go back through the border while you still remember the sun,
while you still remember your own name.
You think I am guarding a lie.
I am guarding a door, and you are what stands on the wrong side of it.
I have stood here for longer than I can count, and I am so tired.
I do not want to fight you.
But if you call me, I will come.

page_16.text: I hold the eye in my hand, and it looks back at me.
My hands do not shake anymore.
They glow so brightly now that the darkness around me looks like daylight.
I keep thinking about the first page of this journal,
about how I wanted to remember the way home.
I cannot remember where home was.
I cannot remember why I wanted to go there.
One more step, and everything ends, and after that, everything will be free.
That is what the voice says, and the voice has never lied to me.

page_17.text: I knew I could not win.
You were stronger than I ever was, because you never fought the voice.
You let it carry you, and it carried you all the way here.
The roots whispered to me too, and I answered with a blade.
I only wanted to hold the line a little longer.
They will call you by my name now.
But not everyone who carries it holds the line.
Nothing stands at the border anymore.

page_18.text: It does not need to anymore.
I looked down into the water, and the water looked back.
Cracks of cyan light, all over my face, all over my arms,
running like rivers on a map.
Dark where I used to be pale.
Bright where I used to be dark.
In my hand there is a black blade.
I do not remember picking it up.
I do not remember when I stopped looking like myself.
I only remember that it felt like coming home.

page_19.text: The Dream Shifter brought me back to the world above,
and the light up here hurts my eyes now.
I sat down in the grass and read this journal again from the beginning.
Every page is in my own handwriting.
The figure at the edge of the mist never came closer.
I lit its pillars and gave its altar the eye and called it down to die.
It only stood between that place and this one, alone,
for longer than anyone should stand anywhere.
It was not guarding a lie.
It was guarding the world from me.
And now there is nobody left to guard it.

page_20.text: Not every story has a happy ending.
